not_for_the_site.why: our own model (class S), Omni-Compass alone (its column C, no Kubernetes) against Kubernetes alone (column A): the mean response time only, while the same column used 40.8% more machine-hours and 25.9% more energy. Not a whole-system gain, not bare metal, not the cloud, and a model is never proof.
the same model's multi-service column: Omni-Compass alone against Kubernetes alone, the mean response time only, with 41.8% more machine-hours and 26.7% more energy. Class S, never a result.

the same model's GPU scenario (class S): Omni-Compass alone against Kubernetes alone, the energy. Not a GPU measurement: the card's own meter reads energy per request served as the chip number above says.
in that model, Omni-Compass on top of Kubernetes (column B) reads the same as Kubernetes alone on web and multi; the model is a tuning bench, not the record.

a 20% operational drain (13% machines + 7% people) is not on the record: the Omni index (20.4%, results/OMNI_INDEX.md) is work, speed and machines on GitHub's machines, not a bill, and the people line measured is the pages (results/OVERSIGHT_PAGES.md), worth about 2% of a run cost at a 7% people share; percentages of different bills do not add.
$16 million is 20% of $100 million; the 20% has no receipt, so neither does the $16 million.
no table, chip receipt or cloud receipt carries a 33% rise in work for the bill.

arm D stands, from the Azure set on file (the four arms above, every gauge paired with arm C); what it cannot show yet is the work per dollar, because that set sent a fixed rate of requests and counted no work. Nor is there a column D in docs/history/model_tables/ABC_TABLE_MODEL.json, so no D may be read from our own model.

no record carries 13.1% as a headline: it appears only inside single rows of the whole-system page's separability check (Kueue's machines on the organism alone; KubeRay's modelled energy), one-row readings on omni-v12 used to test an assumption, never a result to headline.
